question.problem: Find the roots of the polynomial $p(z)=18{z}^{4}+3{z}^{3}-3{z}^{2}.$
question.worked_solution:
To find the roots of the polynomial, we must solve the equation $p(z)=0,$ that is

$$
18{z}^{4}+3{z}^{3}-3{z}^{2}=0.
$$

First, notice that all of the terms of the polynomial have a common factor of $3{z}^{2}.$ We can factor out the $3{z}^{2}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}3{z}^{2}(6{z}^{2}+z-1) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we factor the expression $6{z}^{2}+z-1$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}3{z}^{2}(6{z}^{2}+z-1) & =0 \\ 3{z}^{2}(3z-1)(2z+1) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, by applying the zero product rule, the solutions are $z=0,$ $z=\frac{1}{3},$ and $z=-\frac{1}{2}.$
